capabilities: Log practice sessions with a status-bar timer, quality rating, BPM and review results
Plan sessions for a given time and rank items to practice next
Track mastery levels and run SM-2 based spaced review
Render chord, fretboard, keyboard, scale and ChordPro notation blocks with audio playback
Play and import tabs and scores in alphaTex, Guitar Pro or MusicXML, with metronome and speed control
extras: The user guide lives on an external site rather than fully in the README; notation blocks also render on Obsidian Publish; a public API lets scripts and AI assistants log and plan practice.
motivation: The author is relearning guitar and piano and wanted practice tracking to live next to their other notes, with a system that says what to work on next.
problem: Obsidian has no way to log instrument practice, rank what to work on next, or render and play music notation, so practice material becomes a pile of songs and exercises that never gets revisited.

relations.evidence: drawn by the Music Notation library
Works with the Obsidian Starter Kit (note types, folders, templates and statuses come from it)

summary: Music practice toolkit that logs sessions with a timer, plans what to practice, tracks mastery with spaced review, and renders and plays chord and tab notation.
